prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values and approach
- Reward hard-working families; expand choice; devolve power to professionals and communities; restore accountability.
- Focus on five priorities: cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration, lower taxes.

Economy, tax and pensions
- Cut £12bn a year in waste by 2007-08: £8bn to reduce borrowing (avoid stealth taxes), £4bn for tax cuts.
- Match Labour on NHS, schools, transport and aid; spend more on police, defence and pensions.
- Lower, simpler regulation: restore UK opt-out from the EU Social Chapter; regulatory budgets, sunset reviews; end “gold-plating” of EU rules.
- Maintain Bank of England independence; no to the Euro.
- Pensioner support: halve council tax bills for households where all residents are over 65 (up to £500); link basic state pension to earnings; retain Winter Fuel Payment and other benefits.
- Promote saving: Lifetime Savings Accounts with government top-ups; strengthen company pensions; use unclaimed assets to protect failed scheme members.

Families, childcare and education
- Flexible maternity pay (six or nine months); up to £50/week per under‑5 via tax credit for any childcare type; expand workplace nurseries and after‑school clubs.
- Invest an extra £15bn/year in schools by 2009‑10; restore discipline: heads control admissions/expulsions; Turnaround Schools for disruptive pupils; protect teachers; cut paperwork.
- Money follows the pupil; simpler funding; more rigorous exams (publish marks; end target inflation); allow international qualifications; slim National Curriculum; ban junk food; guarantee two hours of after‑school sport.
- Boost vocational routes: 300,000 grants (£1,000 each) for 14–16s; reform FE (money follows student).
- Scrap university tuition fees; abolish admissions regulator; support university endowments.
- Special needs: moratorium on special school closures; enhance parental choice.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS funding to £2,000 per head; slash bureaucracy (abolish Strategic Health Authorities; reduce PCTs).
- End central targets; empower local clinicians; funding follows the patient; protect community hospitals.
- Bring back matrons; expand single rooms and infection control; aim to end waiting lists; partial NHS contribution for patients choosing private operations.
- Social care partnership so no one must sell their home; more respite and support for carers; reform dentistry; STI public health campaign.
- Health checks for non‑EU migrants staying over 12 months.

Crime, justice and security
- 5,000 extra police officers per year; cut paperwork; elected police commissioners; neighbourhood policing.
- 20,000 extra prison places; end early release; honesty in sentencing.
- Expand drug rehab to 25,000 residential places; reverse cannabis to Class B.
- Homeland Security Minister; robust counter‑terror laws.

Immigration and borders
- British Border Control Police; 24/7 port surveillance; restore embarkation controls.
- Australian-style points system; annual overall immigration limit set by Parliament.
- Asylum processed outside UK; withdraw from 1951 Geneva Convention; take fixed UNHCR quotas.

Constitution, communities, transport, environment
- Abolish regional assemblies; strengthen Parliament; cut MPs by 20%; “English votes for English laws”; devolved choices in Wales; uphold NI consent principle.
- More local say on planning; stronger action on illegal traveller camps.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- End “war on motorists”; modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Protect Green Belt; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; incentives for low‑emission cars; boost recycling; ensure energy security via renewables and efficiency.
- Free vote to overturn hunting ban; support farmers, honest labelling, Little Red Tractor; reform CAP; strengthen animal welfare.

Foreign policy and defence
- Spend £2.7bn more on front-line forces by 2007‑08; preserve regiments; keep NATO central; retain key warships.
- Iraq: remain committed to rebuilding while criticising past handling.
- Europe: oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months, campaign “No”); no Euro; restore Social Chapter opt-out; seek national control over fisheries; support enlargement incl. Turkey.
- Aid: aim for 0.7% of GNI by 2013; more UK control over aid; champion free trade and the rule of law.

Day-one actions
- Start recruiting 5,000 police/year; restore matrons; first Budget to cut waste and lower taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24-hour port surveillance; set EU Constitution referendum date.
